## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Mahākaccānattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 35) is a verse text preserved in the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Pali canon, cataloged within the late sutta strata [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. It commemorates the previous-life aspirations, meritorious deeds, and ultimate spiritual attainment of the elder Mahākaccāna (Mahākaccāyana) [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral indexes five translations of the text across five languages [SuttaCentral].
No curated parallels are identified on SuttaCentral, but automated analysis by DharmaNexus indicates widespread textual reuse within Pali literature, identifying 88 matching segments across 12 Pali texts [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. The text is extensively cited or reused in commentarial literature, exhibiting significant alignments with both volumes of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* as well as the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. It also shares recurrent formulaic verses with other Apadāna poems, including the *Mahāmoggallānattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 4), *Kāḷudāyittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 36), *Asanabodhiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 62), *Padumattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 61), *Rāhulattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 18), and *Bhāgineyyupālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 43) [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus calculates machine alignments with sections of the Sanskrit *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa* and the Tibetan *Ārya-varmavyūhanirdeśa-sūtra* [DharmaNexus].
